title: One Word for One Graph: the Bookseller of Moscia and the Book He Would Not Smooth
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Schooling of a Displaced Boy

stops.name: Velp, birth five weeks before the Armistice
stops.date_confidence: attested. English Wikipedia gives '3 October 1918, Velp, Gelderland' flatly; the coordinate matches OpenStreetMap's Velp, Rheden, Gelderland to within 0.00 km. No civil register or obituary could be reached to confirm the birthplace from a primary document. The research pool's own draft said four weeks before the Armistice; from 3 October to 11 November is five and a half weeks, and the corrected figure is used here.
stops.campa: In Velp, on the flat green shelf of Gelderland where the IJssel comes down to meet the Rhine, a son is born to a Dutch chemist five and a half weeks before the Armistice. They call him Rudolf. Nothing in the household points east. The father's world is the laboratory, and the boy will be steered toward the sciences for as long as anybody else is doing the steering. As an adult he will live in the Netherlands for barely two years, at Leiden, from 1946 until the summer he stops being able to walk.
suggested_refs: The civil registers of Velp, Rheden, Gelderland, for October 1918, not consulted in this research

stops.name: Ober-Hambach above Heppenheim, the Odenwaldschule
stops.date_confidence: the school and the place are attested: German Wikipedia confirms the Odenwaldschule was founded in April 1910 by Paul and Edith Geheeb at Ober-Hambach near Heppenheim, at roughly the coordinate used here. The year 1929 is a reconstruction and is not attested anywhere reached: English Wikipedia says only 'At age 11, Ritsema entered the Odenwaldschule', and 1929 is arithmetic from the 1918 birth year. Month and day are defaulted.
stops.campa: At about eleven he is sent across the German border to Ober-Hambach above Heppenheim, into the school Paul and Edith Geheeb had opened in the Odenwald hills in 1910. No marks are given and nobody is ranked against anybody. Boys and girls are taught together, and the day is built around chosen coursework and manual labor. He is a foreigner here, a Dutch boy in a German valley, and he stays years. The Geheebs take to him and he to them, and their hold on his formation outlasts the school itself.
suggested_refs: The Odenwaldschule buildings at Ober-Hambach, Heppenheim, founded 1910

stops.name: Versoix, the school in exile
stops.date_confidence: attested for the school, reconstruction for Ritsema. German Wikipedia dates the Geheebs' emigration to 1934, not 1933 as the intake dossier had it, and puts the new foundation at Versoix, Canton Geneva, as guests at the Institut Monnier. They leave Versoix in 1936, are at Schwarzsee from October 1939, and reach Hasliberg-Goldern only in May 1946, so the span here is 1934-1936 and not '1934 onward'. That Ritsema himself was at this particular way-station, and met Catherine Gris there, is dossier tradition and independently unconfirmed.
stops.campa: The Geheebs will not teach under the new German state. In 1934 they cross into Switzerland with staff and pupils and set up again above Versoix on the Geneva shore, guests at the Institut Monnier, in what will become the Ecole d'Humanite. Ritsema follows the school into exile. The community he belongs to is now a stateless one, moving from lease to lease along the Swiss lakes, twice more before the war ends. Somewhere near the close of his schooling he meets Catherine Gris, a young music teacher from Geneva.
suggested_refs: The Institut Monnier above Versoix, first Swiss home of the Geheeb school community, 1934-1936
sources: research pool, biographical tradition descended from Shantena Augusto Sabbadini

stops.name: Geneva, biology and the money that stops
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The enrolment in the biology faculty at Geneva, the chemist father's influence, and the wartime interruption of funds from the occupied Netherlands come from the biographical tradition descended from Sabbadini; no University of Geneva matriculation record was located, and no completed degree is documented. The date orders the segment and the coordinate is the historic Bastions campus, not an attested faculty building.
stops.campa: Baccalaureate done, he enrols in the biology faculty at Geneva, following his father's science rather than any pull of his own. Then the war closes the Netherlands and the money from home stops arriving. The studies end without a degree. He is a Dutch student in a neutral city with a blocked account, in a decade that is not going to hand him a profession. No register consulted records what he did in place of the science, or how he lived out the rest of the war. The gap runs from the abandoned faculty year to 1944, and nothing reached fills it.
suggested_refs: The Bastions campus of the University of Geneva, faculty of sciences
sources: research pool, biographical tradition descended from Shantena Augusto Sabbadini
Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.19

stops.name: Casa Shanti, Moscia, the question put to the oracle
stops.date_confidence: the analysis is attested: English Wikipedia states 'In 1944 Ritsema and Catherine Gris began psychoanalysis under Alwine von Keller'. Von Keller's practice at Casa Shanti, seeing patients referred from Zurich, is attested by Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.19 n.3, citing Bernardini, Quaglino and Romano 2015. Two things are unresolved and not resolved here: the pool's chronology places the 1944 analysis at Ascona while its geography lens dates the couple's first Ascona stay to the winter of 1947-48, and the hexagram detail (16 changing to 46) and the 'Who am I' question rest on Sabbadini's memoir alone. The pin is the canonical corpus Eranos coordinate inherited byte-identical from jung.journey.json and olga_frobe_kapteyn.journey.json; independent checking of the Foundation's own address at Via Moscia 125 puts the estate nearer 46.1501/8.7435, and the canon is kept so the pin does not split across the corpus.
stops.campa: Alwine von Keller, once an English teacher at the Geheeb school, keeps a consulting practice at Casa Shanti on the Moscia shore, taking patients Jung sends down from Zurich. Rudolf and Catherine both enter analysis with her in 1944. She has Richard Wilhelm's German I Ging on her shelf and she puts it into his hands. The figures he throws come up sixteen changing into forty-six. Sabbadini, who had it from him half a century later, says the first question he ever put to the oracle was: Who am I?
stops.quote: La primera pregunta de Rudolf al oraculo fue "Quien soy?"
stops.quote_source: Shantena Augusto Sabbadini, biographical sketch of Rudolf Ritsema, shantena.com/en/eranos/rudolf/ (page rendered in Spanish; reached only through the r.jina.ai mirror, the site's own certificate having blocked direct fetching). Diacritics dropped in transcription.
suggested_refs: Casa Shanti, Moscia, Alwine von Keller's consulting house beside the Eranos estate
Richard Wilhelm's I Ging: Das Buch der Wandlungen (Jena, 1924)
sources: Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.19 and n.3

stops.name: Casa Shanti, Moscia, typing the whole first volume
stops.date_confidence: attested in the subject's own book, in a narrative passage written by his co-author: the quoted paragraph is verified piecewise against the Watkins 2005 edition through Open Library search-inside (archive.org id originalichingor0000rudo). The page number p.42 could not be verified, the copy being lending-restricted. The month is a placeholder ordering the segment; only the year 1944 is given by any source. Note the passage spells the analyst 'Alwina von Keller' where every other source has Alwine.
stops.campa: Wilhelm's I Ging is a rare book in wartime Switzerland and von Keller will lend it for a week. Ritsema takes it away and types the entire first volume, working without pause so that a copy of his own exists by the day it has to go back. He is twenty-five. He has no Chinese and nobody to teach him any, and no reason yet to think the book is anything but a private necessity. It will be twenty-seven years before he decides the translation in front of him is wrong. Where the typescript itself went afterwards is not recorded anywhere.
stops.quote: Rudolf Ritsema (b.1918) first encountered the Yi Jing in 1944 through his analyst, Alwina von Keller. Immediately he realized that the book had a central meaning in his life. He borrowed it for a week (the Wilhelm translation was then a rare book, difficult to find in Switzerland during the war years), and, working relentlessly, typed a copy of the whole first volume.
stops.quote_source: Rudolf Ritsema and Shantena Augusto Sabbadini, The Original I Ching Oracle (Watkins, London, 2005), Introduction, 'The Yi Jing at Eranos'
suggested_refs: Ritsema's 1944 typescript copy of Wilhelm's I Ging, whereabouts unrecorded
sources: Ritsema and Sabbadini, The Original I Ching Oracle (2005), Introduction
Open Library search-inside, archive.org id originalichingor0000rudo

stops.name: Geneva, the wedding on the day of the surrender
stops.date_confidence: the date is attested: English Wikipedia gives 'They eventually married on 8 May 1945, when Ritsema was 26', and the coincidence with the German surrender is repeated across sources. The place is inference, not attestation: no source reached names where the ceremony took place, and Geneva is used because it is Catherine Gris's home city. Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.19, confirm her as a Geneva music teacher.
stops.campa: They marry on the eighth of May 1945, the day the German surrender takes effect across Europe, so that the city outside the ceremony is celebrating something other than a wedding. He is twenty-six; she is a working musician. The marriage runs the rest of his life, and she is present at every stage of the work that follows, at the piano and at the door and in the correspondence an entire institution turns out to run on. No source reached names the church or the registry where the ceremony took place, and Geneva is used here because it is her city. Only the day is recorded.
suggested_refs: The Geneva marriage registers for 8 May 1945, not consulted in this research
sources: Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.19

stops.name: Leiden, the antiquarian counter at Brill
stops.date_confidence: attested that the couple moved to the Netherlands a year after the marriage (English Wikipedia) and that Ritsema was working at Brill in Leiden by 1946, its antiquarian book department training him in the Oriental classics (Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi 2020, p.19). The exact title, head of the Oriental department in the antiquarian division, is the intake dossier's wording and was not independently confirmed. The coordinate is central Leiden; the address of Brill's antiquarian division was not located.
stops.campa: A year after the wedding the couple move to the Netherlands, and Ritsema takes charge of Oriental books in the antiquarian division of E. J. Brill at Leiden. He buys and breaks up scholarly libraries, and learns the trade of the book as an object with a provenance and a price. Orientalist rarities and the Chinese classics pass across his counter as merchandise, catalogued and sold on to collectors and university libraries. The I Ching stays a weekend matter, worked at privately, with nothing institutional behind it.
suggested_refs: The antiquarian division of E. J. Brill, Leiden, in the late 1940s
sources: Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.19

stops.name: Leiden, poliomyelitis
stops.date_confidence: attested to the season: English Wikipedia gives 'In the summer of 1947, at the age of 28, Ritsema contracted poliomyelitis'; Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.19, confirm the attack and that Leiden was the couple's residence. The month is a placeholder within that summer. No hospital, physician, rehabilitation regime, or assistive equipment is named in any source consulted, and the paralysis of the diaphragm is reported without a clinical source.
stops.campa: In the summer of his twenty-eighth year he contracts poliomyelitis. The infection reaches the diaphragm and nearly kills him; when it recedes he is paralyzed from the waist down and will not walk again. No hospital, no physician, and no course of rehabilitation is named in anything reachable, across a paralysis that will last fifty-nine years. What is documented is the instruction that follows it, and the instruction is about weather: get out of the Dutch damp, find somewhere warm and dry.
suggested_refs: The 1947 poliomyelitis season in the Netherlands
sources: Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.19

stops.name: Moscia, the winter of the drier air
stops.date_confidence: attested: English Wikipedia dates the meeting with Olga Frobe-Kapteyn to the winter of 1947-48, and the Eranos Foundation's own history page confirms Casa Gabriella as her residence at Moscia since 1920. That the visit was made on medical advice about climate, and that von Keller's neighbouring house is what brought them to this shore, is the biographical tradition, independently unconfirmed. Canonical corpus Eranos pin, inherited byte-identical.
stops.campa: They come south to Lake Maggiore for a few weeks on medical orders, and land beside the one house on that shore where his private obsession is already household currency. Von Keller's Casa Shanti stands next to Casa Gabriella, where Olga Frobe-Kapteyn has lived since 1920 and has run the Eranos conferences since 1933. She consults the I Ching herself, on questions personal and institutional alike, having met it through Wilhelm and the Zurich circle. The few weeks run on into the winter of 1947 and 1948.
suggested_refs: Casa Gabriella and Casa Shanti, Moscia, Ascona, on the Lake Maggiore shore

stops.name: Casa Gabriella, Catherine plays and they are asked back
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction of the scene, attested in outline. Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), pp.19-20, confirm the friendship's founding through music between Catherine and Frobe-Kapteyn and through the I Ching between Rudolf and Frobe-Kapteyn, and confirm that the Ritsemas returned every year for some weeks. That the concert took place in Casa Gabriella specifically, rather than elsewhere on the estate, follows the intake dossier and is not independently pinned down. Month is a placeholder.
stops.campa: At the end of the stay Catherine plays for the house. Frobe-Kapteyn, who built a lecture hall beside her own front door in 1928 and has spent twenty years assembling scholars into it, is taken with the pianist quite as much as with the pianist's husband, and asks them both to come back. A recuperative visit ordered by a doctor becomes an annual appointment, and from now on the Ritsemas spend a month at Moscia every year, lodged near the hall. Which room she played in is not recorded.
suggested_refs: Casa Eranos, the lecture hall Olga Frobe-Kapteyn built beside Casa Gabriella in 1928
sources: Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), pp.19-20

stops.name: Moscia, the month that lengthens into a job
stops.date_confidence: attested in substance, undated in detail. Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.20: 'los Ritsema volverian a Eranos todos los anos durante algunas semanas.' The 1950 date is chosen to order the segment within the attested 1948-1956 span and is not the date of any particular event. Ritsema's later claim that experiential use of the I Ching was among Frobe-Kapteyn's own unfulfilled intentions for Eranos is contested by other participants and is not treated as established here.
stops.campa: For eight years the arrangement stays informal. He is a Leiden bookseller who arrives each summer with his wife, sits at the edge of a conference of orientalists and analysts and historians of religion, and talks with the woman who runs it about a Chinese book they both consult before deciding things. Catherine plays. Rudolf makes himself useful. Frobe-Kapteyn is in her sixties and has named no successor of any kind. Nobody appoints anybody, and nothing about the arrangement is put on paper until 1961.
suggested_refs: The Eranos-Jahrbuch series, published annually from the conferences at Moscia
sources: Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.20

stops.name: Moscia, planning the conferences with Portmann
stops.date_confidence: attested with a one-year discrepancy that is flagged and not resolved: English Wikipedia gives 'In 1956 Ritsema began to collaborate with Froebe and the Swiss zoologist and natural philosopher Adolf Portmann (1897-1982)', while Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.20, date the Ritsemas' participation in organizing the summer conferences from 1957. Nothing reached this pass settles it. Mircea Eliade's presence at Eranos from 1950 and on the 1961 roster is attested in mircea_eliade.journey.json and olga_frobe_kapteyn.journey.json; that Ritsema personally handled his arrangements is inference from the organizer's role, not a documented contact. Month defaulted.
stops.campa: From the middle of the decade he is inside the planning: which subjects, which speakers, in what order, worked out with Frobe-Kapteyn and with Adolf Portmann, the Basel zoologist who has become the conference's intellectual anchor. Catherine takes the household and the music. Among the speakers he now helps house and schedule is Mircea Eliade, at Moscia most summers since 1950. The Dutch bookseller's trade turns out to be exactly the trade an annual conference needs, since somebody has to correspond, invoice, feed, lodge and print. He is thirty-eight and holds no academic post of any kind.
suggested_refs: Adolf Portmann's Eranos lectures and his chair of zoology at Basel
sources: Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.20

stops.name: Casa Gabriella, the will of the twenty-fifth of August
stops.date_confidence: attested verbatim by Tilo Schabert, 'From Olga Froebe-Kapteyn to the Amici di Eranos' (eranos.org PDF), p.2: 'On August 25, 1961 Olga Froebe-Kapteyn wrote up a last will', with the objective quoted here and Portmann appointed 'sole executive of the foundation'. Two corrections to the intake dossier are applied: the will names Portmann sole executive, not president, and it says nothing about the Ritsemas being asked to continue her work as assistants, so that clause is dropped. The place of signature is inference; Schabert names none. Canonical corpus pin.
stops.campa: On the twenty-fifth of August Frobe-Kapteyn writes a last will and founds a second Eranos Foundation to outlive her. Its stated object is the annual conferences and the printed yearbooks, in the spirit she has kept since 1933, and she appoints Portmann sole executive of it. Ritsema is not named in the document. He is nevertheless the man already doing most of the work the document exists to preserve. Schabert, who reproduces the will, lists three provisions in it, and the Ritsemas appear in none of them.
stops.quote: annual Eranos Tagungen held in the same spirit as I have led them since 1933, and the publication of the lectures in the form of Eranos Yearbooks
stops.quote_source: Olga Frobe-Kapteyn's will of 25 August 1961, quoted in Tilo Schabert, 'From Olga Froebe-Kapteyn to the Amici di Eranos: On the history of the Eranos-Tagungen at Ascona' (eranos.org/content/pdf/History_of_Eranos_Tagungen.pdf), p.2
suggested_refs: The 1961 deed of the second Eranos Foundation
sources: Tilo Schabert, eranos.org history PDF, p.2

stops.name: Basel, the Foundation acquires a supervisor
stops.date_confidence: attested verbatim by Schabert (eranos.org PDF, p.2): 'the Eranosstiftung had at first been supervised by the County of Basle. In 1963 this supervision was transferred to the County of Ticino.' The intake dossier's causal gloss, that Basel was chosen as the seat nearest Portmann's university city, is the dossier's own inference; Schabert gives no reason, and the inference is dropped rather than repeated. The month is a placeholder after the August will. Coordinate confirmed against OpenStreetMap Basel to within 0.18 km. This is institutional geography, not a visit by Ritsema.
stops.campa: A Swiss foundation must answer to a supervisory authority, and the new Eranosstiftung is placed first under the County of Basle, then handed on in 1963 to Ticino, where it actually stands. The arrangement looks like paperwork and is not. Everything that happens at Moscia for the next forty years, the conferences and their abolition and the survival of the Foundation that abolished them, will run through a cantonal supervisory file and the single question a supervisor is empowered to ask: is this body still doing what its deed says it exists to do?
suggested_refs: The Swiss foundation-supervision file of the Eranosstiftung, County of Basle 1961-1963, thereafter Ticino
sources: Tilo Schabert, eranos.org history PDF, p.2

stops.name: Casa Gabriella, the death of Olga Frobe-Kapteyn
stops.date_confidence: attested verbatim by the Eranos Foundation's own history page: 'April 25, 1962: Died at Casa Gabriella.' English Wikipedia confirms the consequence: 'when Froebe died in April 1962, the organizational work for the Eranos sessions fell squarely on the shoulders of Rudolf Ritsema'. One contradiction is flagged and not resolved: the Foundation's history page dates Portmann's presidency 1962-1980, while the succession narrative everywhere else runs to his death in 1982. Canonical corpus pin, matching olga_frobe_kapteyn.journey.json.
stops.campa: Olga Frobe-Kapteyn dies at Casa Gabriella in the spring, fourteen years after a piano concert bought the Ritsemas their invitation to come back. Portmann holds the presidency and the intellectual authority; the organizing falls whole onto Ritsema, with Catherine beside him. He is forty-three, a bookseller by training, paralyzed from the waist down, and now answerable for assembling every August a conference of scholars, none of whom answers to him. He holds no title in the Foundation at all.
suggested_refs: Olga Frobe-Kapteyn's grave and the Casa Gabriella estate at Moscia

segments.name: The Yearbooks and the Federal Ordinance

stops.name: Moscia, his name on the yearbook for the first time
stops.date_confidence: a live contradiction between sources, flagged and not resolved. English Wikipedia states that Ritsema 'became editor of the Eranos-Jahrbuch beginning with volume 38 in 1972'. Italian Wikipedia's Eranos article states that Portmann edited the yearbooks 1962-1967, that Portmann and Ritsema co-edited from 1967, and that Ritsema was sole editor from 1981. The intake dossier's correction, that the co-editorship begins with the 1967 conference volume published in 1969 as Polaritat des Lebens, now has this second source on its side, but a library-catalogue check of volume 36 was not possible in this research. Month defaulted.
stops.campa: His name appears on the Eranos-Jahrbuch beside Portmann's for the first time, on the volume of the 1967 conference. The yearbooks are the institution's real body: a conference lasts a week, a volume lasts. Editing them means chasing manuscripts out of scholars working in five languages and holding a house style across disciplines that share no vocabulary, then getting the thing to a printer on a schedule. The sources do not agree on when this began. One dates his editorship from 1967 and another from 1972, and no library catalogue was consulted to settle it.
suggested_refs: Eranos-Jahrbuch 36, Polaritat des Lebens, the 1967 conference volume published 1969

stops.name: Bern, the ordinance from the Department of the Interior
stops.date_confidence: attested verbatim by Schabert (eranos.org PDF, p.3), who quotes the ordinance and dates it to January 1970. The day is not given and is defaulted. This is institutional and legal geography rather than a journey by Ritsema, who is not recorded as travelling to Bern; it is included because the ordinance defines the legal object he later reshapes single-handed.
stops.campa: In January the Swiss Department of the Interior takes the Eranos conferences under its own authority, on the ground that they are international in character. Ritsema is not recorded as having travelled to Bern for any of it. What the ordinance does is write down the fields the Foundation exists to serve, from the study of religions through to Zen and Gnosticism, in language that binds. A private house on a lake now has its purposes fixed by a federal ministry.
stops.quote: Now, in January 1970, the Swiss Department of the Interior in Bern issued an ordinance by which it was determined that the Eranos Tagungen, in view of their international character, would be put under its authority.
stops.quote_source: Tilo Schabert, 'From Olga Froebe-Kapteyn to the Amici di Eranos' (eranos.org PDF), p.3
suggested_refs: The January 1970 ordinance of the Swiss Department of the Interior concerning the Eranos Tagungen
sources: Tilo Schabert, eranos.org history PDF, pp.2-3

stops.name: Moscia, turning against the apparatus
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year: English Wikipedia, 'This reached a turning point around 1971 when he grew dissatisfied with the critical apparatus in the Wilhelm translation.' That he then studied classical Chinese specifically for the project is stated in the same account and is consistent with the method described in his own later introduction, but no teacher, course, or date for that study was found. Month defaulted.
stops.campa: Twenty-seven years after typing it out he turns against the book that formed him. Not against Wilhelm's Chinese, but against the apparatus around it: the smoothing and the Confucian gloss, the German sense poured into the gaps so that a reader meets a finished thought where the original offers a bare graph. He decides the text has to be carried over word by word, one English word held to one ideogram throughout the whole book. Then he begins learning classical Chinese, in his fifties, in order to do it.
suggested_refs: Richard Wilhelm's I Ging and its critical apparatus, the target of Ritsema's revision
sources: Ritsema and Sabbadini, The Original I Ching Oracle (2005), Introduction

stops.name: Moscia, the yearbooks change publisher
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The liquidation of Rhein-Verlag, publisher of the Eranos-Jahrbuch since the series began, and the transfer of the series to E. J. Brill and later Insel Verlag, come from the intake dossier's bibliographic reconstruction and were not independently confirmed in this research. The dossier gives the place as Germany; Rhein-Verlag is generally associated with Zurich, and that discrepancy is left standing rather than adjudicated. The stop is placed at Ritsema's own desk, since what is being described is work he did, not a place he went. Month defaulted.
stops.campa: Rhein-Verlag, which has printed every Eranos-Jahrbuch since the series began, is wound up, and the yearbooks have to be moved to a house willing to take them: first Brill, his own old employer at Leiden, later Insel. The bookseller's decade pays for itself here. He knows what a backlist is worth, what a transfer of rights involves, and how to talk to a publisher as a trade counterpart rather than as a supplicant academic with a manuscript. The series does not miss a volume.
suggested_refs: The Eranos-Jahrbuch imprints: Rhein-Verlag, then E. J. Brill, then Insel Verlag
sources: research pool bibliographic reconstruction, independently unconfirmed

stops.name: Moscia, Portmann's last conference
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. That Portmann fell ill in the late 1970s and could not deliver a planned retrospective address at the 1979 conference comes from the intake dossier's institutional summary and was not independently confirmed. The one-person structure of the Stiftungsrat is separately attested by Schabert (eranos.org PDF, p.5): 'in the case of the Eranosstiftung the Stiftungsrat consisted of just one person.' Month defaulted.
stops.campa: Portmann, eighty-two and failing, cannot deliver the retrospective address he had meant to give the conference. The intellectual authority that has balanced Ritsema's practical authority for seventeen years is going out, and no arrangement exists for replacing it. The council of the Foundation is one man; when that man dies, one man is what remains. What anybody at Moscia thought ought to happen next in 1979 is not recorded, and no successor to Portmann is named in anything that survives from that year.
suggested_refs: Adolf Portmann's unwritten retrospective address for the 1979 Eranos conference
sources: research pool institutional summary, independently unconfirmed
Tilo Schabert, eranos.org history PDF, p.5

stops.name: Moscia, the merger with the Alwine von Keller Foundation
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Eranos Foundation's own history page: 'March 1980: Eranos Foundation merged with Alwine von Keller Foundation'. The same page records that the name reverted to 'Eranos Foundation' in January 2008. The intake pool had this tagged as a dossier-only lead in one lens and as attested in another; the Foundation's page settles it as attested. No day is given. Canonical corpus pin.
stops.campa: The Eranos Foundation absorbs the Alwine von Keller Foundation and carries, for the next twenty-eight years, the names of both women joined. Von Keller is the analyst who took Wilhelm's I Ging off her own shelf at Casa Shanti in 1944 and put it into the hands of a Dutch bookseller who could still walk, and whose consulting house next door is the whole reason the Ritsemas ever came to this shore. The joined name stands on the Foundation's papers until January 2008, when it reverts.
suggested_refs: The Alwine von Keller Foundation, merged into Eranos in March 1980, name reverted January 2008

stops.name: Moscia, sole executive
stops.date_confidence: Portmann's death on 28 June 1982 at Binningen near Basel is attested by English Wikipedia. The succession is attested by Schabert (eranos.org PDF, p.3), who names Ritsema 'the successor of Adolf Portmann in the position of the Eranosstiftung's sole executive', and by Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.20. English Wikipedia frames the whole 1962-1982 span as the Ritsemas keeping the tradition alive single-handedly. The contradiction with the Foundation's own history page, which dates Portmann's presidency 1962-1980, is flagged and not resolved. The stop sits at Ritsema's pin: he was not at Binningen.
stops.campa: Portmann dies at Binningen outside Basel on the twenty-eighth of June. Ritsema succeeds him as sole executive of the Eranosstiftung, and the council of the Foundation now consists of one person, which is himself. He is sixty-three. There is no board to outvote him and no academic body with standing to object. A federal ordinance in Bern describes what the Foundation is for, and he alone decides what satisfies the description. The Foundation's own history page dates Portmann's presidency as ending in 1980, two years earlier, and nothing reached resolves the difference.
suggested_refs: Adolf Portmann's death at Binningen, 28 June 1982
sources: Tilo Schabert, eranos.org history PDF, p.3
Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.20

stops.name: Moscia, Karcher comes to work on the translation
stops.date_confidence: attested to the period: English Wikipedia, 'Towards the end of the 1980s the American poet Stephen L. Karcher assisted Ritsema.' The 1988 date narrows that period to order the segment and is not itself attested; month defaulted. The method described is attested by biroco.com/yijing/contrast.htm, which confirms the base text as 'the same 1715 text used by Richard Wilhelm, transliterated according to Wade-Giles', the one-keyword-per-ideogram rule, and the resulting first English I Ching concordance.
stops.campa: Stephen Karcher, an American poet and mythographer, comes to Moscia to work on the translation. The method is already fixed: the 1715 Palace Edition as base text, one core word held to one graph from the first hexagram to the last, and every occurrence indexed, so that a reader can see everywhere else in the book that a given character stands. It is a translation that declines to read smoothly, on purpose, and a side effect of the rule is the first concordance to the I Ching in English. Six years pass between Karcher's arrival at Moscia and the printed book.
suggested_refs: The 1715 Kangxi-era Palace Edition of the Yijing, base text of the Eranos translation

stops.name: Casa Gabriella, the announcement in the library
stops.date_confidence: attested in detail by an eyewitness: Tilo Schabert (eranos.org PDF, pp.3-4) records that Ritsema 'had asked the speakers at the conference to come together after dinner in a library room of the Casa Gabriella'; that 'Curtly, Ritsema stated that this had been the last Eranos Tagung'; that he would devote himself to the I Ching alone; that Gilbert Durand 'protested against Ritsema's announcement in very strong words, refused to accept it, and spoke of betrayal'; and that Schabert himself argued the Tagungen belonged to no one. Schabert is a participant who later led the breakaway association, so the fullest account available is also not a neutral one. Canonical corpus pin.
stops.campa: After dinner on the twenty-fourth he asks the conference speakers to come to a library room in Casa Gabriella. Standing in front of them he says, curtly and without argument, that this has been the last Eranos Tagung, and that he intends to give himself to the I Ching alone. Ritsema does not debate the point. Tilo Schabert answers that Eranos belongs to no single person, and Gilbert Durand, refusing to accept any of it, speaks in very strong words of betrayal.
suggested_refs: The library room of Casa Gabriella, Moscia, scene of the 24 August 1988 announcement
sources: Tilo Schabert, eranos.org history PDF, pp.3-4

stops.name: Casa Eranos, the concert already arranged
stops.date_confidence: attested by Schabert (eranos.org PDF, p.4): 'Arrangements had been made for a piano concert this evening to be given by Catherine Ritsema... in the Ritsema's spacious living room at the Casa Eranos.' That the timing was designed to foreclose deliberation is the interpretation of Schabert and other participants, not a stated intention of Ritsema's, and is presented here as their reading. Casa Eranos is a separate building from Casa Gabriella; both sit on the same estate and share the canonical corpus pin.
stops.campa: A piano concert has been arranged for that same evening in the Ritsemas' large living room at Casa Eranos, and the speakers are sent to it directly from the announcement. Catherine plays. The men who have just been told that the institution they have given thirty years to no longer exists sit through the music in a private drawing room with no chance to confer. Whether the scheduling was meant to stop them conferring is a question the participants answered one way and Ritsema never answered at all.
suggested_refs: Casa Eranos, the Ritsemas' residence and the Foundation's lecture hall
sources: Tilo Schabert, eranos.org history PDF, p.4

stops.name: Casa Eranos, Hornung on Akhenaten and the buses outside
stops.date_confidence: attested by Schabert (eranos.org PDF, p.4), who quotes Hornung's closing sentence, describes the uproar, and records Ritsema's response. The intake dossier had mistakenly described Hornung's lecture without its subject; it was on Echnaton, that is Akhenaten. Schabert's account is eyewitness testimony from the side that went on to found the rival association, and is used with that caveat. Canonical corpus pin, standing for the Eranos lecture hall.
stops.campa: The next morning Erik Hornung lectures on Akhenaten and closes by telling the hall what has been decided and what he makes of it. His last sentence is that the fundamentalism which heaves up its head everywhere today has no future. The audience erupts. Ritsema ends the disturbance not by answering it but by pointing at the clock: the buses that serve the lake road are outside and leave in five minutes. The hall empties on that timetable, fifty-five years after the first conference. It is the twenty-fifth of August, 1988.
stops.quote: The buses have arrived, they depart in five minutes!
stops.quote_source: Rudolf Ritsema, ending the uproar in the Eranos lecture hall, 25 August 1988, reported by Tilo Schabert (eranos.org PDF, p.4)
suggested_refs: Erik Hornung's 1988 Eranos lecture on Akhenaten
sources: Tilo Schabert, eranos.org history PDF, p.4

stops.name: Moscia, the circular that claims the whole Foundation
stops.date_confidence: attested by Schabert (eranos.org PDF, p.5), who dates the mailed announcement of the new I Ching project to the autumn of 1988 and sets it against the report Ritsema filed with the supervisory authority. The month is a placeholder within that autumn. That the lecture hall was built by Frobe-Kapteyn in 1928 is attested by the Eranos Foundation's history page.
stops.campa: In the autumn he mails a circular announcing that the Foundation entire is to be given over to a new project on the I Ching. There is no consultation, because there is nobody he is obliged to consult. The lecture hall his predecessor built in 1928 will go on standing; what stops is the thing it was built for, a yearly public gathering of scholars from unrelated disciplines talking to an audience. He is sixty-nine. The circular does not say for how long.
suggested_refs: The autumn 1988 Eranos circular announcing the I Ching project
sources: Tilo Schabert, eranos.org history PDF, p.5

stops.name: Moscia, two documents that do not agree
stops.date_confidence: attested by Schabert (eranos.org PDF, p.5), who describes the 1989 report to the Stiftungsbehorde asking for a pause to find a successor and clarify finances, sets it against the autumn 1988 circular, and names the tension. Schabert does not state from where the report was filed; Moscia is the reasonable default rather than an attested location. The founding of the Associazione Amici di Eranos is separately attested by Schabert, pp.6-7: a meeting of twelve on 11 February 1989 at the Hotel Al Porto, Ascona, and the formal founding at the Hotel Tamaro, Ascona, on 31 October 1989. That founding is the other party's scene and is cited here, not staged. Month defaulted.
stops.campa: His report for 1988 to the Swiss supervisory authority explains the suspension as a pause: he needs time to find a successor and to clarify the Foundation's finances. The circular he had already posted that autumn said something different, that the Foundation was being converted whole to the I Ching. Both documents are his. The supervisory file records a pause; the mailing list records a conversion. Along the lake road in Ascona, the people he dismissed in August spend the year building an association of their own.
suggested_refs: The Associazione Amici di Eranos, founded at the Hotel Tamaro, Ascona, 31 October 1989
The Eranosstiftung's 1988 report to the Swiss supervisory authority
sources: Tilo Schabert, eranos.org history PDF, pp.5-7

stops.name: Moscia, eighteen people around a table
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. That public conferences resumed at Moscia in October 1990, partly because Swiss foundation statutes require continued activity, and that the Round Table form seated roughly eighteen people for three days around a personal question and a cast of the oracle, come from the intake dossier's institutional reconstruction and were not independently confirmed. Schabert independently confirms the competing scale: the breakaway Amici held their own first conference at Casa Serodine, Ascona, from 19 August 1990, with two hundred attending. The quote is from the 2005 book and states the principle, not words spoken in 1990.
stops.campa: Public sessions start again at Moscia, small ones, because a Swiss foundation that does nothing is a foundation with a problem. What resumes is not what stopped. Instead of a lecturer and an audience there are about eighteen people in a room for three days, presenters and invited participants together, each session built on one personal question and one cast of the oracle. The platform is gone, and the person asking is not permitted to be a spectator. Down the lake at Ascona that same August, the breakaway association opens its own first conference to an audience of two hundred.
stops.quote: It is crucial to realize that the responsibility for all choices always rests with the consultant herself or himself.
stops.quote_source: Rudolf Ritsema and Shantena Augusto Sabbadini, The Original I Ching Oracle (Watkins, London, 2005), Introduction
suggested_refs: The Eranos Round Table sessions, Moscia, 1990-2002
Casa Serodine, Ascona, where the Amici di Eranos held their rival first conference from 19 August 1990
sources: research pool institutional reconstruction, independently unconfirmed
Tilo Schabert, eranos.org history PDF, pp.7-8
Ritsema and Sabbadini, The Original I Ching Oracle (2005), Introduction

stops.name: Moscia, Sabbadini joins the work
stops.date_confidence: the collaboration is attested by English Wikipedia: 'Together with Shantena Augusto Sabbadini (b. 1943), the Italian physicist and spiritual thinker, he produced the first Italian rendering.' The 1991 start date is the intake dossier's and was not independently confirmed; month defaulted. The quote is the first of the four rules for consulting the oracle printed in their joint introduction of 2005.
stops.campa: Shantena Augusto Sabbadini, an Italian physicist, joins him to make the Italian version. The collaboration outlasts every other working relationship of Ritsema's life and produces, in the end, the fullest statement of what the Eranos translation thinks it is for: not prediction, not a rulebook, but an apparatus for making the person who consults it do their own thinking in the presence of an image they did not choose. Sabbadini is a physicist by training, forty-eight years old, and comes to the text without a sinologist's stake in how it has always been rendered.
stops.quote: Ask only questions that are emotionally significant for you.
stops.quote_source: Rudolf Ritsema and Shantena Augusto Sabbadini, The Original I Ching Oracle (Watkins, London, 2005), Introduction, 'Interrogating the oracle', rule 1
suggested_refs: Shantena Augusto Sabbadini's Eranos I Ching work, 1991 onward
sources: Ritsema and Sabbadini, The Original I Ching Oracle (2005), Introduction

stops.name: Moscia, one word for one graph
stops.date_confidence: the method is attested in the translators' own printed introduction and independently described by Steve Marshall at biroco.com/yijing/contrast.htm ('each ideogram is translated throughout by the same key word', producing 'the first English I Ching concordance'). The 1993 date carries no event; it orders the segment between the start of the collaboration and the 1994 publication. Month defaulted.
stops.campa: The rule is absolute, and it is what makes the book strange. One Chinese graph, one English word, everywhere it occurs, whether or not the sentence reads well as a result. The English stops being a substitute for the Chinese and becomes a code for it, and the concordance at the back turns the whole text into a searchable field of recurrences. Readers raised on Wilhelm's German fluency find the result close to unreadable, and reviewers of the English edition say so in print.
stops.quote: Each Chinese ideogram is translated consistently by the same English word, which becomes a sort of code identifying the ideogram.
stops.quote_source: Rudolf Ritsema and Shantena Augusto Sabbadini, The Original I Ching Oracle (Watkins, London, 2005), Introduction, 'Basic features of the Eranos translation, Core-words'
suggested_refs: The Eranos core-word concordance method
sources: Ritsema and Sabbadini, The Original I Ching Oracle (2005), Introduction

stops.name: Shaftesbury, Element Books prints the concordance
stops.date_confidence: attested for the imprint: the Eranos Foundation's own I Ching page gives 'I Ching, The Classic Chinese Oracle of Change, The First Complete Translation with Concordance, translated by Rudolf Ritsema and Stephen L. Karcher, Element Books, Shaftesbury/Rockport/Brisbane'. The intake dossier had wrongly placed it at Moscia in one lens and at London in another. The 816 pages, the 1715 base text and the method are confirmed by biroco.com/yijing/contrast.htm. This is a publication-place marker: Ritsema is not recorded as having travelled to Dorset, and month and day are defaulted.
stops.campa: Element Books brings the joint work of Ritsema and Karcher out of Shaftesbury in Dorset: eight hundred and sixteen pages, the first complete translation with concordance, built on the same 1715 text Wilhelm had used. Fifty years after typing a borrowed copy in a week, he has produced a rival to it, and it divides its readers at once between those who find it unusable and those who find every other version unbearably smooth. Ritsema is not recorded as ever having gone to Dorset. The imprint reads Shaftesbury, Rockport, Brisbane.
suggested_refs: I Ching: The Classic Chinese Oracle of Change (Element Books, 1994), 816 pp.

stops.name: Moscia, the presidency handed over
stops.date_confidence: attested with a wobble in the date. English Wikipedia says only 'In the early 1990s Ritsema passed on the presidency of the Fondazione Eranos'; the Eranos Foundation's history page lists Christa Robinson as president 1994-2001; Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.20, say Robinson moved from Zurich to Ascona expressly to take administrative work off Ritsema, and that he went on making the major decisions until 2002. Both the 'early 1990s' and the 1994 figure are reported and neither is adjudicated. Month is a placeholder.
stops.campa: His health is failing and the administration is more than one paralyzed man can carry. Christa Robinson, an analytical psychologist, moves down from Zurich for the express purpose of taking the office work off him, and becomes president of the Foundation. Ritsema keeps the decisions. For the next eight years the presidency is hers on the letterhead and his in fact, an arrangement nobody at Moscia writes down and everybody at Moscia understands. When exactly the handover happened is given as 1994 in one place and as the early 1990s in another.
suggested_refs: The Eranos Foundation presidency of Christa Robinson, 1994-2001
sources: Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.20

stops.name: Moscia, the parting with Karcher
stops.date_confidence: attested in Karcher's own words, quoted at length by Steve Marshall at biroco.com/yijing/ritsema.htm; the sentence about revisions sits inside Karcher's block quote, not in Marshall's prose, and is therefore Karcher's characterization of Ritsema and not a reviewer's paraphrase. The 1996 date is the intake dossier's and is not itself attested; month defaulted. Ritsema's own account of the break was not found in any source reached. The quoted passage reproduces the source's own duplicated word, 'the the'.
stops.campa: He and Karcher separate over the text they made together, each holding a right to use the original material. Karcher's account is that Ritsema would not entertain revisions of any kind, and that he himself took a publisher's offer to make them. Ritsema's account of the break has not been found in anything reachable. What follows is two descendant versions of one book, revised in opposite directions by two men who no longer discuss it. Both of them keep the concordance.
stops.quote: Mr Ritsema and I have more or less parted company, each having a 'right' to use the the original material. He has independently published Italian and German small press editions of the original text, but has steadfastly maintained he was not interested in revisions of any sort.
stops.quote_source: Stephen Karcher, quoted in Steve Marshall's review, biroco.com/yijing/ritsema.htm
suggested_refs: The two descendant editions of the 1994 text, Karcher's revision and the Ritsema-Sabbadini revision

stops.name: Turin, the Italian edition
stops.date_confidence: a bibliographic contradiction, flagged and not resolved. The intake dossier gives Eranos I Ching: Il libro della versatilita from Red Edizioni at Como in 1996, with an expanded UTET edition the following year. The Eranos Foundation's own I Ching page lists the Italian editions as 1997 UTET, Torino, and 2011/2017 URRA/Feltrinelli, Milano, with no 1996 Red Edizioni entry at all. The stop follows the Foundation's own bibliography and is placed at Turin; the Como edition is recorded as unsupported by the project's own list rather than denied. Publication-place marker: Ritsema is not recorded as travelling to Turin. Month defaulted.
stops.campa: The Italian version made with Sabbadini appears from UTET in Turin. It is the first of the translation's children in another language, and it carries the Round Table decade inside it: seven years of watching people at Moscia put real questions to the book have changed what the editors think the apparatus around the text is for. The Chinese base has not moved a character; everything built around it has been rebuilt for a reader sitting at a table with a question they mind about. A 1996 Como edition is reported elsewhere and appears nowhere in the Foundation's own list of its editions.
suggested_refs: The 1997 UTET Turin edition of the Eranos I Ching
The disputed 1996 Red Edizioni, Como, edition, absent from the Foundation's own bibliography

stops.name: Munich, the book returns to German
stops.date_confidence: attested for the imprint by the Eranos Foundation's I Ching page: 'Eranos Yi Ching. I Ging. Das Buch der Wandlungen, translated by Rudolf Ritsema and Hansjakob Schneider, O.W. Barth, Muenchen' (2000). The date at which Schneider joined the project, given as 1997 in the intake dossier, is dossier-only and unconfirmed. Publication-place marker: Ritsema is not recorded as travelling to Munich. Month defaulted.
stops.campa: Hansjakob Schneider, a Swiss linguist, works the same material into German, and O. W. Barth publishes Eranos Yi Ching: Das Buch der Wandlungen at Munich. When Schneider joined the work is given as 1997 in one account and confirmed by none. German is the language in which he first read the oracle, fifty-six years after he sat typing Wilhelm's volume against a one-week loan. The new edition does not translate Wilhelm and does not set out to correct him in public. It stands on the same shelf, in the same language, doing the opposite thing.
suggested_refs: Eranos Yi Ching: I Ging, Das Buch der Wandlungen (O. W. Barth, Munich, 2000)

stops.name: Moscia, the Periplus of the Eranos Archetype
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, and the weakest evidential link in this file. The unpublished manuscript, its title, its twenty-one theses and its ending in the dissolution of the Foundation as a legal entity into the esoteric archetype of Eranos are reported in the intake dossier from Hans Thomas Hakl's account; the manuscript itself was not locatable for direct citation, and no independent confirmation was reached. The date orders the segment and carries no event; month defaulted.
stops.campa: In his eighties he writes something he does not publish: a manuscript called The Periplus of the Eranos Archetype, reported to advance twenty-one theses and to end by proposing that the Foundation as a legal entity dissolve into what he calls the esoteric archetype of Eranos. A periplus is a coasting itinerary, a sailor's list of landfalls taken in order. He has spent fifty-two years on one shore of one lake, and the itinerary he finally sets down closes by asking the institution to stop existing.
suggested_refs: The unpublished manuscript The Periplus of the Eranos Archetype, location unrecorded
sources: research pool, reporting Hans Thomas Hakl; manuscript not located, independently unconfirmed

stops.name: Moscia, the last Round Table season
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction for the sessions, attested for the handover year. That the Round Tables ran through 2002 at three or four sessions a year is the intake dossier's institutional reconstruction, independently unconfirmed; that Ritsema went on making the major decisions until 2002 is attested by Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.20. The Foundation's own history page lists the successors after Robinson as Wanda Luban, Maria Danioth, John van Praag and Fabio Merlini. Month defaulted.
stops.campa: The Round Tables run their last season, fourteen years after the form was imposed on a furious body of scholars who wanted the lecture hall back. Three or four times a year through the whole of the 1990s, a room of eighteen has turned on a question somebody brought and an image the book returned. He is eighty-three, and he lets go of the decisions as well as the office. After him the presidency runs through Wanda Luban, Maria Danioth, John van Praag and Fabio Merlini.
stops.quote: There are no rules for interpreting these texts. They do not have an intrinsic meaning, independent from you and from your question.
stops.quote_source: Rudolf Ritsema and Shantena Augusto Sabbadini, The Original I Ching Oracle (Watkins, London, 2005), Introduction, 'Reading your answer'
suggested_refs: The Eranos presidents after Ritsema: Wanda Luban, Maria Danioth, John van Praag, Fabio Merlini
sources: Manas Penalver and Loredo Narciandi (2020), p.20

stops.name: London, Watkins prints the last book
stops.date_confidence: attested: the onlineclarity.co.uk review of the Ritsema-Sabbadini edition places The Original I Ching Oracle: The Pure and Complete Texts with Concordance at Watkins Publishing, London, in 2005. The quoted sentence is verified through Open Library search-inside of the Watkins edition (archive.org id originalichingor0000rudo); the intake pool had rendered it as a standalone capitalized sentence, which does not occur, and the verbatim form given here restores its opening words. Page numbers could not be verified, the copy being lending-restricted. Publication-place marker: no visit to London is recorded. Month defaulted.
stops.campa: Watkins publishes The Original I Ching Oracle in London, by Ritsema and Sabbadini: the 1994 text again, but with the concordance method explained rather than merely applied, and fifteen years of Round Tables folded into the instructions for use. It is the last major book of his life, and the only one in which he says plainly, in an introduction meant for strangers, what he thinks he has been doing since 1944. Four rules are printed there for consulting the oracle, and one sentence for what the book is: a mirror of the present.
stops.quote: In this sense we use the Yi Jing as a mirror of the present.
stops.quote_source: Rudolf Ritsema and Shantena Augusto Sabbadini, The Original I Ching Oracle (Watkins, London, 2005), Introduction, 'A mirror of the present'
suggested_refs: The Original I Ching Oracle: The Pure and Complete Texts with Concordance (Watkins, 2005)
sources: onlineclarity.co.uk, review of the Ritsema-Sabbadini edition
Open Library search-inside, archive.org id originalichingor0000rudo

stops.name: Moscia, the eighth of May again
stops.date_confidence: the date is attested: English Wikipedia, 'He died on 8 May 2006, at the age of 87, on the 61st anniversary of his marriage to Catherine Gris.' The place is not. Neither the Eranos Foundation's history page nor any other source reached states where he died, of what, or where he is buried, and no tomb or memorial was located; Moscia is used as the default because it was his home for fifty-eight years, and the gap is a real hole in the public record rather than an omission here. Canonical corpus pin.
stops.campa: He dies on the eighth of May 2006, eighty-seven years old, sixty-one years to the day after the wedding that fell on the German surrender. Where he died and of what are not established by anything reachable, and no tomb or memorial notice has been located. The Foundation's own history page disposes of his fifty-eight years on the estate in a single line about presidents succeeding one another. Six weeks later, at a gathering there, Robert Temple is reported to have used the occasion to say what he had shut down and whom he had shut out.
suggested_refs: Robert Temple, 'Eranos: Past and Future', address at the June 2006 Eranos gathering, text not located in this research

segments.name: What Is Left on the Shelves

stops.name: Lugano, the Fondo Rudolf Ritsema
stops.date_confidence: attested for the collection, undated for its constitution. The Sistema bibliotecario ticinese lists 'Fondo Rudolf Ritsema [LUMC] [WLC=LUMCritsema]' at the Biblioteca del Museo delle Culture, Lugano. The coordinate is corrected from the intake pool's central-Lugano figure to OpenStreetMap's placement of the Museo delle Culture at Riva Antonio Caccia 4a, Pambio-Pazzallo. No source states when the fondo was constituted; a date shortly after his death is assumed to order the segment, and the month is a placeholder. This stop is posthumous.
stops.campa: His personal library is taken into the Ticino library system as a named collection, the Fondo Rudolf Ritsema, held at the Museo delle Culture in Lugano and searchable under a code of its own. These are the books a Leiden antiquarian bought and kept over sixty years, catalogued at last by somebody else. With no grave found, the shelf list is the one solid physical trace of him outside the estate. Nothing in the catalogue records when the fondo was constituted, or who decided that it should exist.
suggested_refs: Fondo Rudolf Ritsema, Biblioteca del Museo delle Culture, Lugano, catalogue code WLC=LUMCritsema

stops.name: Lugano-Besso, two hundred and sixteen tapes
stops.date_confidence: attested verbatim on the Eranos Foundation's audiovisual collection page: 'The Swiss National Sound Archives keep 216 magnetic audiotapes, donated by the Eranos Foundation in 2009', covering 1968 to 1998. The coordinate is corrected from the intake pool's figure to OpenStreetMap's placement of the Fonoteca Nazionale Svizzera at Via Soldino 9, Lugano-Besso. The page does not say which recordings carry Ritsema's own voice. Month and day defaulted. This stop is posthumous.
stops.campa: The Foundation gives two hundred and sixteen magnetic tapes to the Swiss National Sound Archives at Lugano-Besso. They run from 1968 to 1998 and cover almost exactly the span of his editorship and his directorship, including the years after the voices on them stopped being invited. How much of Ritsema himself is on the tapes, as against the speakers he recorded, is not stated anywhere in the donation record. What he ended in one evening in a library room survives here as three decades of other people's voices, on reels, in a suburb of Lugano. The record gives a count, a date range, and nothing else.
suggested_refs: The 216 Eranos audiotapes, 1968-1998, Fonoteca Nazionale Svizzera, Lugano

stops.name: Cordoba, a fourth language
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Eranos Foundation's own I Ching page, which lists the 2022 Spanish edition, I Ching: El libro de los cambios. El proyecto del I Ching de Eranos, credited to Ritsema, Sabbadini and Maria Cruz Manas Penalver, Editorial Cantico, Cordoba, and presents it as the most recent descendant of the project. The page count of over a thousand comes from the same framing. Month and day defaulted. Publication-place marker and posthumous by sixteen years.
stops.campa: A Spanish edition comes out of Editorial Cantico at Cordoba, credited to Ritsema, Sabbadini and Maria Cruz Manas Penalver: more than a thousand pages, sixteen years after his death and twenty-eight after the first English volume. The core-word rule survives passage into a fourth European language. The conferences he closed have never reopened under the Foundation's name, and the book he closed them for is still being reset and printed. Cordoba is a city he never saw, in a country he is not recorded as having visited.
suggested_refs: I Ching: El libro de los cambios. El proyecto del I Ching de Eranos (Editorial Cantico, Cordoba, 2022)
